exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
comps: None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ATCL repertoire list for drum kit, read from the Trinity PDF (37 entries). Programmes must have a minimum of two works and may include own-choice pieces (pre-approved); only one chart-based item (marked *) may be included; for FTCL at least one listed work is required. Scores must be fully realised, electronic kits are not allowed, no more than half the programme may be solo, backing tracks must be used at original speed and without original drums, and click tracks may only be heard through headphones/in-ear monitors (ATCL/LTCL exception where no click-free track exists). Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.
